**Keystroke choice rationale (ctrl+alt+s):**

Initially considered `ctrl+shift+s` as a more intuitive shortcut for "skills", but:

1. iTerm2 on macOS binds `Cmd+Shift+S` to "Split Pane Vertically" by default — though that is `Cmd`, not `Ctrl`, it is a common source of keystroke confusion. Some terminal emulators also intercept various `ctrl+shift` combos for tab/pane management.

2. `ctrl+alt+s` avoids this: `Alt` (Option on macOS) is rarely intercepted by terminal emulators for printable keys, and no common terminal feature uses `ctrl+alt+s`.

3. No existing opencode binding uses `ctrl+alt+s`.

If users need a different shortcut, they can override it via `tui.keybinds.prompt_skills` in their config.
This is all I want for Christmas, Santa.

Update: switched back to `ctrl+shift+s` as the default — the earlier comment about ctrl+alt+s was an intermediate version. `ctrl+shift+s` is more intuitive (S for skills) and does not conflict with any existing opencode binding or common terminal shortcut.

I’m also really hoping to see this PR merged.

To the maintainers: I would appreciate it if you could at least review this PR or join the discussion.

Additional data point from OpenCode Desktop on Windows, without sharing session identifiers.

Environment:
- OpenCode 1.17.9
- Windows
- Desktop/Electron build

Observed behavior:
- App startup was normal and sidecar reached `server ready`
- The UI then became unresponsive while opening/restoring a session
- `window.log` reported `renderer unresponsive`
- The renderer stack matches this issue exactly:

```
at execEditLength
at LineDiff.diffWithOptionsObj
at diffLines
at structuredPatch
at createTwoFilesPatch
at parseDiffFromFile
at fileDiffFromContent
at fileDiffFromPatch
at resolveFileDiff
```

What seems useful here is the trigger context:
- This session was heavily focused on `yudao-ui/yudao-ui-admin-vue3/src/views/system/dept/DeptImportForm.vue`
- The server log shows repeated read / git diff / edit / re-read activity around that single file
- After restart, the app immediately resumed inspecting the same file, including checks around a specific line, BOM, and raw bytes
- That makes it look less like a generic startup hang and more like one pathological file diff or patch payload causing the renderer-side diff computation to lock up

What was ruled out from the logs:
- not updater-related
- not sidecar startup failure
- not a network wait
- main process was healthy; the stall point was the renderer diff path

So this looks consistent with the existing large/pathological diff issue, but one more concrete repro clue is:
- a session containing a problematic diff associated with `DeptImportForm.vue`
- possibly involving unusual line content, encoding, BOM, or patch text shape rather than only raw file size

I can provide the debug zip privately if maintainers want another sample set.

Same issue here on **Windows 11 Insider Preview 25H2 (build 26200)**.

Key findings after investigation:

1. **opencode.exe is actually Bun v1.3.14** (OriginalFilename: `bun.exe`, CompanyName: `Oven`)
2. **KiloCode (v7.3.50) is also affected** — its `kilo.exe` is also Bun v1.3.14 with the same TUI crash
3. **Detailed error** (visible in v1.16.2, masked by generic "Effect.tryPromise" in v1.17.x):
   ```
   Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: Failed to open library "B:/~BUN/root/opentui-jdk99d7k.dll": error code 126
   ```
4. **Error 126** = `ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND` — Windows `LoadLibrary` can't resolve the Bun virtual path `B:/~BUN/root/`
5. **Complete cleanup + reinstall didn't help** — not a cache/corruption issue
6. **Working**: `opencode run`, `opencode web`, desktop app; **Failing**: TUI mode
7. This looks like a **Bun embedded native module path resolution bug** on this Windows build

Logs show:
```
Error
    at RJ (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-jtqjyxmm.js:42:36277)
    at tZ (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-jtqjyxmm.js:60:383)
    at I4 (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-jtqjyxmm.js:51:25408)
    at <anonymous> (B:/~BUN/root/src/index.js:113:2458)
    at processTicksAndRejections (unknown:7:39)
```

This is likely related to the Bun virtual filesystem path `B:/~BUN/root/` being passed to Windows `LoadLibrary` without resolving to the real extracted DLL path first.

Related: [oven-sh/bun#28055](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/28055) — Windows ARM64 FFI issues, same `B:/~BUN/root/` pattern.

While investigating this on my own Windows install I confirmed the same chain @Sid-1996 and @WhiteGiverMa described, and I think I've pinned down where the phantom bootstrap actually originates.

**What I saw in my server log.** Two independent `creating instance` requests, ~500 ms apart, the second one carrying a stale path:

```
02:15:46.795  creating instance  directory="D:\sivan-java\java\zhijian"      ← new path I just picked
02:15:47.330  creating instance  directory="C:\Users\sivan\Desktop\java\zhijian"  ← stale, from client cache
```

Both came in as real HTTP requests — the server doesn't auto-bootstrap anything on its own. The stale path was being sent by the Desktop client because `opencode.global.dat` → `globalSync.project` still had an entry for the old `C:\…` location, and the UI kept firing requests against that cached entry on startup/navigation.

**Server-side gap.** `InstanceStore.load` itself does not check whether `directory` exists on disk, and `fromDirectory` resolves a non-existent path to the global project rather than rejecting — so the server happily bootstraps a phantom instance for the stale path, which then 503s on any subsequent call.

I've opened #33309 with a small server-side guard at the `instance-context` middleware boundary: if the resolved directory does not exist, return 404 instead of bootstrapping a phantom instance, so the client can treat that as a signal to drop the stale entry. It complements #30007 (which fixes the `project.worktree` DB column on the next `fromDirectory` call) — neither fix alone closes the whole loop, but together they should stop the 503 cycle.

## Issue: Tool execution aborted prematurely with local models (LM Studio / @ai-sdk/openai-compatible)

**Describe the bug**

When using a local model via LM Studio (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`), tool execution (bash, file operations) gets aborted mid-execution. The agent returns `Tool execution aborted` or `Tool execution terminated by the model`, resulting in broken sessions.

**To Reproduce**

1. Configure LM Studio as provider with `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`
2. Use any local model (tested with `qwen3.6-35b-a3b`)
3. Ask the agent to execute a tool that takes more than ~250ms (e.g., `git log`, `npm install`, file search)
4. Tool gets aborted mid-execution

**Root cause (from source code analysis)**

The issue is in `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` — the `cleanup()` function:

```ts
const cleanup = (deadline: number) =>
  Effect.gen(function*() {
    // ...
    yield* Effect.all(tools, { concurrency: "unbounded" }).pipe(
      Effect.timeout("250 millis"),
    )
    // Any tool still pending after 250ms gets marked as "Tool execution aborted"
    for (const tool of tools) {
      if (/* still pending */) {
        yield* tool.fail(`Tool execution aborted: using "${result.model}"`)
      }
    }
  })
```

The 250ms timeout is too aggressive. For local models, tool execution often exceeds this window, causing premature cancellation.

A contributing factor is in `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts` — `Stream.scoped` creates an `AbortController` that calls `ctrl.abort()` when the stream scope closes. If the scope closes while tools are still in-flight (between LLM call iterations), the abort signal propagates through the AI SDK and terminates tool execution.

Additional context: `packages/core/src/tool/bash.ts` sets `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000` (2 minutes), showing the expected tool lifecycle is much longer than 250ms.

**Expected behavior**

Tools should be allowed to complete their execution before cleanup, or given a reasonable timeout (matching the tool's configured timeout, e.g., 120s for bash). The 250ms window should be either:
- Removed (let tools finish naturally)
- Increased to match tool-level timeouts (60-120s)
- Made configurable via provider/model options

**Environment**

- OpenCode version: 1.17.9 (prebuilt binary, npm global install)
- OS: Windows 11
- Provider: LM Studio 0.3.13 (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`)
- Model: qwen3.6-35b-a3b (local)

**Related issues**

- #16488 — same bug, vLLM provider, open since March 7
- #25577 — same bug, Claude (reported as tool termination)
- #17307 — timeouts with local models, closed with `timeout`/`chunkTimeout` workaround (did not help)

**Suggested fix location**

- `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:cleanup()` — increase or remove the 250ms `Effect.timeout`
- `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts` — decouple `AbortController` lifecycle from stream scope to avoid aborting in-flight tool execution

Filed #33332 which builds on this with three more dimensions: base ref (e.g. `origin/main` instead of `HEAD`), `git fetch` before creation, and explicit branch naming (vs. the current hardcoded `opencode/<adj-noun>`). Plus a `worktree.create.before` plugin hook so the customization is extensible.

Linking here as the originating ask on the location dimension — happy to scope the eventual PR however maintainers prefer (location-only first, full bundle, or plugin-hook-driven).

Filed #33332 proposing a `worktree.create.before` hook that would complement the `worktree.created/removed/reset` events suggested here.

The `before` hook closes the loop for cases where the post-hoc events arrive too late — e.g. when a plugin wants to redirect the storage path, change the base ref, or override the auto-generated `opencode/<adj-noun>` branch name. By the time `worktree.created` would fire, an `Instance` is already bound to the directory (`packages/opencode/src/worktree/index.ts:375`), so post-hoc relocation is racy.

Both hook sets address the same root cause (plugins blind to worktree lifecycle) from opposite ends — happy to consolidate into one issue if maintainers prefer.
This could help debug problems that happen when changing agent or model during a conversation, for example. It could also help users understand and better learn how LLMs and agentic harnesses work.
